interest: Occupation use of Perry and Harris commemorations.
overview: State Department decimal file 894.415 covers commemorative celebrations held in post-World War II occupied Japan between July 1947 and September 1948. The collection primarily documents the participation of American occupation authorities and Japanese officials in public ceremonies that linked historical US-Japan diplomatic milestones with contemporary occupation objectives. Prominently featured are materials detailing the July 1947 revival of the 'Black Ship' Festival at Shimoda commemorating Commodore Matthew Perry and Townsend Harris, General Douglas MacArthur's August 1947 address to the Hiroshima Peace Festival on the atomic bomb anniversary, Acting Political Adviser William J. Sebald's July 1948 address at the Kurihama Perry landing memorial, and MacArthur's September 1948 statement marking the third anniversary of V-J Day. Across these dispatches, speeches, press releases, and newspaper clippings, American officials and Japanese elites utilized commemorative occasions to emphasize post-war demilitarization, constitutional democracy, economic reconstruction, and Japan's strategic alignment with the Western democracies amidst the emerging Cold War.
